subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw add a core enforced execution-progress contract for artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and post-green follow-through, or keep this limited to existing loop/stale-run guardrails plus smaller bug fixes?
rationale: The request aligns with runtime reliability, but it adds new enforcement policy, persistence, configuration, telemetry, and user-visible behavior that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core guardrail design
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design tracker and require an MVP that reuses runner/diagnostic events, SQLite state, and measured telemetry before enabling enforcement.

options.title: Split only concrete bugs
options.body: Track specific reproduced tool-loop, stale-run, or timeout bugs separately and defer artifact-gated status enforcement until live traces justify it.

options.title: Decline broad enforcement
options.body: Close the direction as too policy-heavy for core and continue relying on existing loop detection, post-compaction guards, stale-run recovery, and operator monitoring.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core guardrail design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design tracker and require an MVP that reuses runner/diagnostic events, SQLite state, and measured telemetry before enabling enforcement.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest product/routing candidate from recent loop-detection docs and agent runtime guardrail history, though implementation ownership is shared.
